title: splitext("archive.tar.gz") gives you ".gz", not ".tar.gz"
assumption: The 'extension' of a filename is everything after the first dot.

input.description: Any compressed-archive filename, used to decide how to decompress an uploaded or downloaded file.

what_goes_wrong: Code that branches on the file's extension to pick a decompressor sees only ".gz", runs gunzip, and is left holding a .tar file it never un-tars — or mis-identifies the file type entirely.
why: Both os.path.splitext and Node's path.extname define 'the extension' as the text from the LAST dot to the end of the string, a deliberate choice so a filename like "version.1.2.3" isn't treated as having the extension ".1.2.3". That same rule means a genuinely double-barreled extension like ".tar.gz" is reported as just ".gz"; the ".tar" part is silently folded into what both functions report as the base name.
fix: For known compound suffixes (.tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz, ...), check against an explicit list of multi-part suffixes before falling back to splitext/extname.

test_cases.note: An extension detector used to pick a decompressor must recognize compound archive suffixes; splitext/extname alone return only '.gz'.
